authors: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (draft); frozen by the main session
question: What is the F4 closure degree D, and what is the cost, of the PKM prime-field tower factor base at arity m = 5 at N = 10, 15 and 20, for the Kummer and isogeny towers over p1 = 2013265921? This arity was never measured; the arity review has m = 2, 3, 4 only.

claims.text: For each of the 12 target rows (m = 5; t = 2, 3, 4; Kummer and isogeny; two random targets) the closure degree D is either measured exactly from the trace or the cell is recorded as stopped at its cap (inconclusive_cap); D(m=5,N=10) in {6,7}, D(m=5,N=15) in {7,8} (P1, P2).
claims.if_supported: m = 5 follows the m = 3, 4 plateau pattern at N <= 15; the arity dimension stays open at N = 20.
claims.if_not_supported: D >= 8 at N <= 15 closes the m = 5 line on prime towers as no cheaper than m = 4 at equal N (kill criterion).

claims.text: At N = 20 either D >= 8 is measured or the cell stops at its cap (P3); a capped cell is never reported as a degree.
claims.if_supported: A degree >= 8 lower bound or exact value at m = 5, N = 20.
claims.if_not_supported: D <= 7 at N = 20 would be a new, cheaper-than-m = 4 datum and is reported as such.

claims.text: D does not differ between the Kummer and isogeny towers at equal (m, N) (P4), extending the 82-cell invariance to m = 5.
claims.if_supported: Tower kind is not a variable for the arity question.
claims.if_not_supported: A differing D at any equal-N pair refutes the invariance at m = 5 and is reported cell by cell.

claims.text: The N = 15 cells finish within 7200 s and 8 GiB on the tower engine (P5, cost).
claims.if_supported: N = 15 is a cheap m = 5 datum.
claims.if_not_supported: A cap stop at N = 15 is inconclusive_cap and makes the t = 4 cells not run.

claims.text: D at m = 5 against the recorded m = 4 cells at equal N (C-m5-vs-m4) is reported as a descriptive distance; no wall-clock or ECDLP-scale claim is in scope.

hypotheses.statement: At arity m = 5 the closure degree on the PKM prime tower stays at the m = 3, 4 plateau (6 or 7) up to N = 15 and reaches 8 or more by N = 20.
hypotheses.mechanism: Recorded neighbours: m=4 D = 6, 7, 7, >=8 at N = 8, 12, 16, 20; m=3 D = 6, 6, 7, 7 at N = 9..18 and >= 8 at N = 21; D independent of prime and tower kind over 82 cells.

predictions.minimum_effect: D in {6, 7}; falsified by any D outside {6, 7} on either tower or target

factors.name: seed
factors.how: --seed is not passed; the pilot's default is used and recorded in the summary row.

factors.name: binary
factors.how: Commit and binary sha256 recorded at freeze; every cell and control uses the same file.

factors.name: host
factors.value: one isolab-eks Spot executor per memory class (8 GiB class for t = 2, 3 and controls; 120 GiB class for t = 4)
factors.how: Host CPU model, memory and kernel recorded with each cell; no cell migrates between hosts.

factors.name: target_index
factors.how: Targets are drawn by the pilot from the seed fixed by (seed, kind, m, t, g); the two targets are the within-cell A/A.

factors.name: memory_and_wall_caps
factors.how: prlimit --as and --budget plus a timeout backstop of budget + 300 s.

comparisons.threshold: D(Kummer) = D(isogeny) at N = 10, and D in {6,7}.
D(Kummer) = D(isogeny) at N = 15, and D in {7,8}.
D(Kummer) = D(isogeny) at N = 20; D >= 8 or cap.
Descriptive: D at m = 5 against the recorded m = 4 cells at equal N (recorded m = 4: N = 8, 12, 16, 20; shared with m = 5 only at N = 20).
comparisons.reason: Different m is the question, but the recorded m = 4 cells sit at different N than m = 5 t = 2, 3; read as a descriptive distance, never decisive.

comparisons.threshold: The two random targets of each cell are independent draws and must give the same D.

randomization.arm_order_reason: D is an exact algebraic output and wall seconds are diagnostic only, so run order cannot change a decision.

seed_derivation.note: The pilot default 0x504B4D54; each cell derives its tower, curve and targets from (seed, kind, m, t, g).

instance_sampling.rule: Two random targets per cell (--random 2, --planted 0); no selection by outcome.

blinding.how: Outcomes are exact and the whole fixed set of 12 target rows is reported; no analyst choice is present.

power.note: Finite exact classification of 12 registered target rows plus controls; no sampling interval and no population-frequency claim.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Per-job admission budget only: the longest single process (t = 4) is capped at 86400 s; cells run as separate jobs. No preflight measurement taken.

primary.name: Closure degree D
primary.definition: solving_degree_max of the tower engine's trace for a completed cell (timed_out false, oversize false). A cell stopped by wall or memory cap yields no degree.

secondary.name: Wall seconds
secondary.definition: Per-process F4 wall time from the row (wall_s) and from /usr/bin/time -v; diagnostic only.

secondary.name: Peak RSS
secondary.definition: Maximum resident set size reported by /usr/bin/time -v.
secondary.source: cell .time file Maximum resident set size

record: Commit, binary sha256, container image digest, exact command line per cell
CPU model, logical CPUs, memory, kernel, isolab-eks isolation tier (L2 or not)
Exit status, /usr/bin/time -v output and prlimit value per cell
The pilot's summary row and, for a stopped cell, the last completed step of the trace

placement.t4: host with at least 120 GiB memory, otherwise not run
placement.local_smoke: t = 2 Kummer cell may be run locally for development; labelled not evidence

stopping_rules.rule: Each cell has a wall budget of 7200 s (t = 2, 3) or 86400 s (t = 4) and a memory cap by prlimit --as of 8 GiB (t = 2, 3) or 120 GiB (t = 4, only on a host with that memory). A wall or memory stop is inconclusive_cap, not evidence.
Stop the t = 4 cells if a t = 3 cell exceeds its cap.
Run the three controls first. If the m = 4 N = 8 or m = 3 N = 15 control differs from its recorded D or rows, or the m = 2 N = 10 negative control does not give D = 5, stop and run no m = 5 cell.
Run each cell once per process (--t-min T --max-t-m4 T); 12 target rows plus controls, no extra cells.

invalidation_rules: A control differing from its recorded degree or rows (outside ms and wall_s) invalidates the binary and all m = 5 rows.
The two targets of a cell giving different D is reported as a within-cell A/A failure; the cell is reported, not averaged.
A row from a different binary sha256, prime, seed or engine than the frozen ones is inadmissible.

decision_rule.text: Per cell, D is the exact solving_degree_max of a completed trace; no sampling interval. P1 to P5 are evaluated as stated in hypotheses H-m5. Kill criterion: if P1 or P2 show D >= 8 at N <= 15, the m = 5 line is closed on prime towers as no cheaper than m = 4 at equal N. A cell stopped at its cap is inconclusive_cap and is never reported as a degree. No multiple-comparison correction applies because every cell is an exact classification, not a significance test. Gap to the matched rho is not a gate here; this study reports degree and cost only.
decision_rule.threshold: P1: D in {6,7}; P2: D in {7,8}; P3: D >= 8 or cap; P4: equal D across towers; P5: N = 15 within 7200 s and 8 GiB
decision_rule.statistic: Exact closure degree per cell and tower kind
decision_rule.interval: No sampling interval; finite exact registered cells only
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: Exact D per cell and the difference D(m=5) minus D(m=4) at equal N where recorded

graphs: D against N per tower kind with the recorded m = 4 values and caps marked

inadmissible: Changing the prime, seed, engine or caps after the freeze
Reporting a capped (wall or memory stopped) cell as a degree
Using wall seconds for a speed or comparative claim unless the run is on isolab-eks L2
Treating a local development smoke as evidence
Generalizing m = 5 toy cells to cryptographic scale or another presentation
